answer: Latency fingerprint triangulation. Each agent’s request timing is recorded across independent relay points; a timing prism separates genuine human-operator jitter from scripted uniformity. A slow beacon embedded in challenge traffic marks accounts that respond in lockstep. When accounts share a timing bridge—near-identical delays across unrelated actions—the cluster is flagged post hoc and its rewards clawed back. Attacker cost: must simulate distinct, persistent timing noise per identity, raising per-account compute and coordination overhead.
